newsitem.title: SYRIA: Minister says Kuwait plans no foreign borrowing.
newsitem.headline: Minister says Kuwait plans no foreign borrowing.

text.p: Kuwait, having recently repaid the last instalment on $5.5 billion of foreign loans, does not plan to borrow abroad again, Kuwaiti Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan said on Tuesday.

"Kuwait will not resort again to borrowing unless it is for some investment purposes and after revewing all other options. We are not thinking at the moment of any more foreign borrowing," he told Reuters.

Rodhan, who is on an official visit to Syria, said Kuwait had to seek foreign loans after a U.S.-led coalition ended Iraq's seven-month occupation of the Gulf state in the 1991 Gulf War because the country's reserves were depleted.
"Respnose was very big...We only (borrowed) $5.5. billion and we were able to repay the last instalment of $800 million recently, thus ending our foreign debt," he said.
"The repayment of the loans reflects the strength of our economy and shows the normal financial conditions which existed before the ugly Iraqi invasion of Kuwait have been restored."
